selectivity_statement.phase1: the base model assumes infinite selectivity and no numeric selectivity is available in the library
selectivity_statement.phase2: Required ideal H2/N2 selectivity for Grade D (N2 300 ppm, R 0.90, 1 bar permeate, 400 degC): 12919. Sourced: Cechetto et al. 2021 state above 400,000 (double sealed) and above 500,000 (dead end) at 450 degC; the printed double-sealed N2 permeance gives about 40,541. The requirement is met by every sourced value, but only as ideal (single-gas) values of NEW membranes from one group, at 450 degC, with trace NH3 only; mixed-gas and aged selectivity were not found (a review excerpt reporting decay 6000 -> 4300 and 4300 -> 1000 in about 1000 h could not be opened and is not used).
selectivity_statement.nus_researchers: Zhang Sui and Zhao Dan are membrane scientists at NUS Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering. Their verified published gas-separation work is on non-metallic membranes at low temperature and does not address cracked-ammonia purification. No number from their work is used in AmCraX and no specific work is attributed to them here (research/notes/nus_membrane_researchers.md)

csv_column_notes.capital_USD: Fixed purification capital other than membrane modules, charged with the capital recovery factor plus maintenance and insurance: the PSA + TSA units for PSA; for the membrane only the NH3 polishing bed (Grade D only, an adsorber-share proxy). Zero for the industrial-grade membrane, which needs no polishing bed.
csv_column_notes.membrane_module_cost_USD: Purchase cost of the Pd-Ag membrane modules (area x cost per m2). Not part of capital_USD: it is annualised over the membrane life with the capital recovery factor at that life.
csv_column_notes.replacement_USD_per_yr: Annualised membrane module cost (area x cost per m2 x capital recovery factor at the membrane life); it covers the module replacement.

membrane_central.cause: NH3 polishing bed (measured permeate NH3 2.9 ppm > 0.1 ppm limit); bed cost is a proxy

abdoos2025_sourced_case.description: Abdoos et al. 2025 (simulated front for a dry, NH3-free cracked-ammonia composition) as a labelled sourced case beside Yanez 2020 (different feed), the mass-balance assumption and 0.85. Nothing existing is replaced.

abdoos2025_sourced_case.evidence_grade: simulated (Aspen Adsorption, ANN surrogate, NSGA-II); no cyclic-PSA experiment
boundary_differences: adsorption pressure 7.9-11.6 bar at the optima (bounds 6-12 bar) against the AmCraX 19.5 bar PSA feed; the paper's own trend (higher pressure: higher purity, lower recovery) makes the extrapolation to 20 bar not neutral
dry, NH3-free 75/25 H2/N2 feed (NH3 and H2O are not model components) against AmCraX cracked gas with about 1 % NH3 and water upstream of the TSA
purity is the N2 impurity only; Grade D also needs NH3 <= 0.1 ppm, which the paper leaves out of scope
simulation and surrogate: recovery scatter about 1-3 points at 72-78 % recovery (Fig. 13); whether Table 8 values are surrogate or full-order outputs is not stated
feed 83-98 kmol/h against about 198 kmol/h; optimum feed temperature about 10 degC against 40 degC
the paper's specific energy (6.4-8.76 MJ/kg) is feed compression from about 1 bar; it is not used (AmCraX needs no feed compressor at 19.5 bar)

H4-a.assumptions: AmCraX has no adsorption-cycle model; the PSA recovery at any purity is an input
H4-a.uncertainty: Grade D recovery 0.555 (Yanez, different feed) to 0.81 (Mehr, low confidence); for a cracked-ammonia composition only a simulated front exists: Abdoos 2025, 0.7744 at 99.99 % and 0.8192 at 99.95 % (dry, NH3-free feed, 11.3-11.6 bar, surrogate scatter about 1-3 points)
H4-a.reason: the direction is shown by two literature sources (literature_comparison), not computed: Yanez 2020 (measured, ammonia-plant purge gas) and Abdoos 2025 (simulated, dry NH3-free cracked-ammonia composition; its model equations and breakthrough check cite Yanez 2020, so the two are not fully independent); the AmCraX relation is flat by construction. Computed for the membrane instead: at a fixed sourced selectivity, permeate N2 rises with recovery (P2-MEM-1), but this row is about PSA

H4-b.proposed_verdict: SUPPORTED (direction), narrow envelope; the evidence matrix rule decides

H4-b.assumptions: PSA recoveries are inputs; polishing-bed cost is a proxy (adsorber share); delivery 30 / 350 bar
H4-b.uncertainty: factorial over all sourced inputs (PSA recovery, CAPEX basis, electricity, membrane cost, life, selectivity, flux, recovery)
H4-b.envelope: 20 bar baseline cracked gas, grey NH3 450 USD/t, electricity 0.084-0.222 USD/kWh, unified basis
H4-b.threshold: none needed for the sign: the Grade D increment of the cheapest route is positive in every input combination; its purity-only part at equal delivery is small (membrane: polishing bed; PSA: about zero under the flat relation, positive under Yanez)
H4-b.reason: ordering raw < cheapest industrial < cheapest Grade D holds at every electricity price and every sourced input combination (order_holds_everywhere = True). Caveat: raw < industrial is structural (raw skips purification) and most of the Grade D increment is 350 bar delivery, not purity; the evidence matrix rule may judge the purity-only part too small or too proxy-dependent and keep INCONCLUSIVE

H4-c.reason: published composition fails the 99.9 % index and Grade D (secondary row, does not vote)

H4-d.assumptions: membrane housing, skid and heating CAPEX not modelled (favours the membrane); PSA own power and TSA heat not modelled (favours PSA); permeate at 1 bar
H4-d.uncertainty: factorial over sourced inputs; ranking reverses inside it
H4-d.envelope: membrane cheaper only if PSA Grade D recovery is below about 0.783 (central membrane) or 0.745 (high-cost membrane)
H4-d.threshold: PSA recovery at parity 0.745-0.783 (Grade D; high-cost to central membrane) and 0.749-0.795 (industrial); sourced PSA values straddle it (0.555 Yanez, different feed, below; 0.81 Mehr, low confidence, above; Abdoos 2025, simulated for this composition, 0.7744 at 99.99 % lies between the two Grade D parities and 0.8192 at 99.95 % above both industrial parities). Membrane cost (parity 28,824 USD/m2 against the central PSA) and life (parity 0.95 yr) are outside the sourced ranges, so they do not decide the ranking; selectivity requirement 12,919 is below all sourced ideal values. Membrane annualised with CRF(i, life)
H4-d.reason: the ranking is decided by an unsourced PSA recovery; readiness also differs: Pd-Ag downstream separator TRL 4 to 5 against PSA unit 9 / integrated chain 6 to 7; Ammogen did not meet its recovery KPI. Secondary row, does not vote

H4-e.proposed_verdict: INCONCLUSIVE (fix pass 24 Nov 2026: the direction restates the flowsheet's tail-gas routing; the threshold recovery is the finding and sourced recoveries 0.555-0.85 straddle it)

H4-e.uncertainty: computed for recoveries 0.50-0.95 (PSA and membrane trade-off grids)
H4-e.envelope: 20 bar baseline; above recovery 0.765 the tail gas does not cover the furnace and NH3 is burned; below it the lost H2 has no use in this flowsheet
H4-e.reason: computed energy balance; holds for both technologies (same threshold, since it depends only on the H2 sent to the furnace)
